summary.title: Programming Projects for Advanced Beginners #4: Photomosaics
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a photomosaic generator that rebuilds an input image from many small source images matched by average RGB colour, then speed it up with caching and bucket indexing.
takeaways: Split the input image into about 50x50 squares and compute each square's average RGB colour, then pixellate as a warm-up.
Crop source images to squares, compute their average colours, and pick the nearest match per square using Euclidean distance in RGB space.
Cache source-image average colours in a JSON file, and use a per-image cache to avoid stale data.
Build an index that maps rounded RGB values to buckets of source images so each match compares far fewer images.
Extend matching by comparing average colours of image quarters and combining the distances.
summary.summary: This is a project-based tutorial for advanced beginners that walks through building a photomosaic creator in any programming language. It lays out a seven-step plan: load and manipulate an input image, split it into squares and average their RGB colours, crop a set of source images to squares, match each input square to the nearest source image by Euclidean RGB distance, and paste the chosen images into an output image. The extensions cover speeding things up with JSON caching, a rounded-RGB bucket index, and finer matching by comparing image quarters.
